utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. May the record reflect that this late start is due to technical problems. Could you call the case, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-04-75-T, the Prosecutor versus Goran Hadzic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. May we have the appearances starting with the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. Douglas Stringer, Alexis Demirdjian, and Case Manager Thomas Laugel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. For the Defence, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Zoran Zivanovic and Chris Gosnell for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. We go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So OTP calls its next witness, which is 091. Is that right, Mr. Demirdjian?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: 75, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: 75. Yes, indeed. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Witness. Thank you for coming to The Hague to assist the Trial Chamber. First of all, do you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Could you please tell us your name, your date of birth, and your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Milan Miladinovic. 2nd February, 1955.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And your ethnicity, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Serb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. You are about to read the solemn declaration by which witnesses commit themselves to tell the truth. I have to point out to you that the solemn declaration that you are about to make does expose you to the penalties of perjury should you give misleading or untruthful evidence to the Tribunal. Please read the solemn declaration now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may be seated. Mr. Demirdjian, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this be turned up, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. The witness needs the volume to be turned up. He --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's okay now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Great.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Miladinovic.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, it is correct to say that you have been met by the Office of the Prosecutor in May of 2001 and that you gave a statement on that occasion; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can we pull up the statement, please? It is 65 ter 2449.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And you will see, Mr. Miladinovic, the statement appear on the screen in front of you to your right. On the right-hand side you will see, I believe, the English version, and on the left-hand side you will see the statement in the Serbian version. Do you see them?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now in 2001, when you gave this statement, it was first written in English and it was read back to you in your language; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And at the bottom of the English version --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: If we could scroll down.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I believe that your statement appears there.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now you were also met by members of the Office of the Prosecutor in September this year; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And we discussed matters relating to the content of your statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now in relation to this statement you gave in May 2001, is this statement -- does this statement accurately reflect your evidence?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And if you were asked the same questions today in the courtroom, would you give the same answers?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, could I ask for the witness's statement to be admitted, along with the associated exhibit? There is one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 2449, witness's statement, shall be assigned Exhibit P267. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Miladinovic, when you arrived in The Hague, you were also shown the proofing note which was made in September when you were visited by members of the Office of the Prosecutor. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And you read this statement. You were given an opportunity to review it; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And you had one clarification to make in relation to this proofing note, and I will ask you a question about it now. In your statement you make references to the -- to where Goran Hadzic was stationed in Dalj. Now the proofing note states that he was stationed in the department store near the main street, and I think you wish to correct that. Could you tell us where he was stationed in Dalj?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Next to the department store there is the shop of Bozidar Masaric, just next door to the department store.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And is that where he had -- where he was stationed?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's where he was supposed to be stationed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now at page 3 of your statement you explain, and you describe the attack on Dalj on the 1st of August, 1991. And you say that: "We knew that the attack would be launched on 1 August 1991, but we were not sure about the time." Can you first of all clarify --

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could you first of all clarify for the Trial Chamber who you mean when you say "we," "we knew the attack would come"? Who do you mean by "we"?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we in the village. Most everyone already knew that there would be an attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And how did you know that the attack was imminent? How was that information conveyed to you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there was a number of people who constantly commuted to Borovo and Dalj and through them the news reached us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And could you tell the Trial Chamber who were these people?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they were closer to the SDS, those people who travelled unhindered even by the Croatian police at the time, so they were able to go back and forth. And it's from them we learned that an attack was coming. We didn't know exactly when but we knew it was coming. The rumour was all around the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now during the attack where were you exactly?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I was at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And what did you hear during the attack exactly?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand. What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sorry. Let me take you to your statement at page 3. You say that the attack started at 4.00 in the morning: "... and later on I learned that the assault was launched from the direction of Borovo." So perhaps the better question is: Did you hear anything during the attack?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we could hear the shooting when the attack began.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And again coming back to my question about who knew about the attack, you told us that the SDS members conveyed this information to you. Did they inform -- well, who did they inform? Did they inform everyone in the municipality or members of -- oh, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: No, the -- that was not the case that anybody informed anybody. It's those people who were on good terms with everyone. People shared the news and that's how eventually we all learned that an attack was imminent.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now after the attack, you mention that -- in your statement at page 3, you mention the creation of the TO staff in Dalj and you explain that the commander was Pavle Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now on this page you also provide a number of names. And I'd like to bring your attention to the name Djorde Calosevic, aka Briga. Did you know this person before the war?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I knew him. Not that well, but I knew him. He wasn't in Dalj all the time. He was in Bosnia for a while. Then he came to Dalj. Then he worked for a while in Osijek. I knew him slightly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And here you say that when the TO staff was created he became -- or was involved, actively involved with the TO command; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And could you tell us whether -- well, what was his role, if you know, in the TO command?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I think he was president of the municipality. At that time Dalj was a municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you know whether he's still alive today?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I think he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And do you know where he lives?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I know that he's across the border in Serbia but I don't know where exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now you mention at page 4 of your statement that you kept working for IPK Dalj after the attack of the 1st of August; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Were you asked to join the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. Nobody asked me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So you remained an employee of IPK Dalj; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could you tell us who your superior was in IPK Dalj?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: My superior was Dragan Lovric.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And was he -- did he remain your superior after the attack?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And could you tell the Trial Chamber where your offices were in Dalj?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Within the compound in one of the offices.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And could you tell us where the compound was located in Dalj?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: The company itself is not far from the railway station, on the periphery of Dalj, as you go towards Osijek.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I would like to show you a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Which is 65 ter 6241. And this is at tab 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Miladinovic, you will see in a moment a map or an aerial image of the village of Dalj, and with the help of the usher I would like you to identify the location of IPK Dalj. Do you see the map in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Are you able to locate the IPK workshop and the offices on this aerial image?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can you circle it? Okay, can you place a -- can you circle the area of the IPK workshop?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And this is the office which is near the railway station; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can you mark with a number 1 where the railway station is, if you are able to see it on this image?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And for the sake of the completeness, could you mark the IPK with number 2.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could I ask for this image to be seized and marked, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 6241, marked by the witness in court, shall be assigned Exhibit P269. Just for the record, the associated Exhibit 2450 was assigned Exhibit P268.267. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, later in your statement - and I will come to that - you talk about the events at Lovas farm, and you mention hangars where people were kept from Vukovar. Are those hangers visible in this image?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: The hangar is at Lovas. You mean that one?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I mean the hangars where people were brought from Vukovar. You state in your statement that people were held in Dalj.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Those are the hangars.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So this is the same location that you had marked as number 2 in the previous image; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: We don't need to tender this image. We already have it on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, sir, after the JNA and the TO took control of Dalj, you told us that -- well, can you tell us first of all what happened to the non-Serb population in Dalj?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Let me rephrase my question. You explained to us that on the 1st of August there was an attack on the town and that the TO staff was created. After this 1st of August, can you tell the Trial Chamber what happened to the non-Serb population, so the Croats, Hungarians, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: They were in labour platoons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And did they all remain in Dalj?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So did there come a time where non-Serbs from Dalj were taken somewhere by boat?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: The only people who left Dalj -- the only non-Serbs who left Dalj went to Osijek from Aljmas by that ship.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And what proportion of the non-Serb population left from Aljmas by ship?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I think 90 per cent left.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, at page 3 of your statement, you mention a man by the name of Milorad Stricevic and you indicate that he was put in charge of interrogation of non-Serb villagers, those who remained in Dalj. Can you tell us when you heard that Stricevic was put in charge of interrogations?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that was on the second day, when those people from the SDS came from Bogojevo [as interpreted], they immediately set upon deciding who's going to be whom in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And just to be perfectly clear, what do you mean by "the second day"?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I mean the second day of the attack. It was known immediately who was going to be in charge of questioning, another one was president of the municipality, a third one was the main man in the village. That was the second day after the attack, when the municipality was being established.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Before the conflict, did you know where Stricevic was from?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Stricevic was from Dalj.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say in your statement that he was in charge of interrogations, could you tell us what you heard about these interrogations?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: He was in charge of interrogating those people who had been arrested, who had been on the Croatian side and were then arrested. He was in charge of conducting their questioning, to get them to say some things about Croatian plans. That's, I believe, what the questioning concentrated on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And did you hear about how he conducted this questioning?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the questioning was normal between Serbs and Croats. The questioning was the sort of questioning you have when there is a war going on. There were beatings and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I'd like to move on to the part of your statement where you explain how you were ordered to bury bodies in a few instances. The first instance you mention is the five bodies that were discovered on the road to Trpinjska Cesta. You explained this was in September or October, and you explained in your statement as to how you helped digging a hole for the burial of five Croats. Now, in your statement you say that when you were helping out with the burial, you did not know the reasons, but you later learned that these men were killed by Arkan. Could you tell the Trial Chamber how much time after the burial of these five Croats you learned of Arkan's involvement?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I learned about it. When I finished work, when I returned home in the village, it was known that Arkan was heading towards Vukovar, that he killed those people and left them in the cornfields.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So you say you learned this when you returned home in the village.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Just to establish the time-period, how much time after you returned to the village did you hear about this?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, it was in the morning at around 9.00. I was digging. My shift ended about 1.00 or 2.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now you mention that you were asked to help out with this burial by, again, Mr. Djordje Calosevic. Did Mr. Calosevic make any comments during the burial?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Objection. We have no notice of the content of this testimony in the proofing note or the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Demirdjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Let me get back to that, Your Honours. I'll strike that question for now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Miladinovic, I'd like to move now to the events at -- that you describe about the Lovas farm. Now in this second -- in this instance you explain that you were ordered by Pavle Milovanovic to drive your excavator to Lovas farm; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could I ask that we display on the screen 65 ter 6242, which is at tab 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Miladinovic, we are going to now look at another aerial image of the area around Dalj. In the meantime, could you tell us what is the distance generally between Dalj and Lovas farm?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. 4 kilometres or 2 or 3 kilometres. Not more than that. 3 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can I ask that we zoom a little bit on the bottom half. And scroll all the way down.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: On this aerial image, Mr. Miladinovic, are you able to locate Lovas farm, roughly?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: This part here. Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could you mark that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: It keeps zooming in, I think, instead of marking.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That's it. This area here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can we zoom up, please, before the witness marks it. Thank you. So let's zoom in again the bottom half, just to have a bit of perspective. A little bit more. Just a little bit more. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can you mark it now, Mr. Miladinovic.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And can you tell us which road you took with the excavator to make your way to Lovas farm?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: You can't see it here. You can't see it in this photograph, but it would be more or less here. From the beginning and then in this direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now we see that Lovas farm is located close to the river and you've made a little marking to the right. So we see a marking to the right and we see a main road. You did not take the main road. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, when you go from Dalj to Borovo it's on the left. Now it's to the right when you go towards Dalj. I'm referring to the farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And just to make this clear, which road do you take to go from Dalj to Borovo?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: When you go from Dalj to Borovo, the farm is on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. And is that the road you took?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can I ask this map to be marked, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 6242, marked by the witness in court, shall be assigned Exhibit P270. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now when you arrived at Lovas farm, sir, you tell us that along with Milovanovic there are two men there. I should say three, sorry. You mention Mr. Zeljko Pajic and man named Calosevic, aka Fafrika, and you mention a third man whose name you did not know. Starting with Zeljko Pajic, can you tell us who he was and what functions he occupied in Dalj?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: They were in the SDS. As for his function, I don't know what his official position was but I do know that he was a member of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And you say you don't know his function. Did you know which organisation he worked with -- sorry, he worked for?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And the second person, Calosevic, whose nickname is Fafrika, can you tell us who he was? Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: They were also in the SDS. They were closer to the SDS, together with Pajo, so naturally they performed all those duties together with Pajo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now you say in your statement that once you arrived you saw bodies lying on the ground and that it appeared that they were killed only recently. When you arrived there, how were the -- well, how were the bodies? Where were they?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were on the grounds of the farm scattered around, very recently killed, allegedly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And if we could pull up, actually, 65 ter 6278.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You will see now, sir, an image of this area. You have already marked or drew a sketch of this, so I will not ask you to indicate again every location. Do you recognise this image, first of all?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And can you tell us what it is? What are we looking at?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this is the farm. The grounds of the farm. This is the area where the bodies were buried. This is where I buried them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now show us the entrance of the farm? Can you mark it with a number 1.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand that. What location were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The entrance to the farm.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: The entrance. Somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And when you entered the farm, in which area were the bodies located?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: The bodies were even further away on the grounds of the farm. If I can show you like this, it would be somewhere around here. That's where the bodies were located.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could you mark that with a number 2.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: When you enter the farm, you pass by an office, and you turn left. There was a sort of field toilet there, and that's where these bodies that had been killed were scattered, in the vicinity of that toilet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Right. And this area, could you mark it with a number 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I am to mark it with number 2, the location where the bodies were found?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now the road that we see on this image from where you enter Lovas farm, can you tell us which road is this?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the road is here. You enter the farm from the road. That's how I entered with the excavator. There is an asphalt road here behind the office and in front of the office, and you can use it -- or, you can travel down this road to get as far as the field toilet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Let me rephrase that. I am talking about this road that we see from where you entered. Where you marked the number 1, there seems to be a road going from north-south. Could you tell us what that road is?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: This road continues to Osijek. This one goes on to Borovo, and the one to the left leads to Osijek.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have about ten more minutes. Is this the appropriate time for the break or?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is, but we should clarify about the road because I am not sure that the witness understood what -- what you were exactly asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You were asking about the road that goes from the top of the image to the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. But we'll come back to that after the --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And in the meantime, maybe we could seize the image --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: -- to make sure we don't lose the information and mark it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 6278, marked by the witness in court, shall be assigned Exhibit P271, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Witness, we will take a break now and come back at 12.45. The Court Usher will escort you out of court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Demirdjian. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Miladinovic, the image should still be on the screen before you. We just wanted to clarify this main road again. You told us that it goes to Borovo and to Osijek. So where would Borovo be located in relation to this area?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Borovo is somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: For the record, you're pointing towards the south; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now going north, which is the first village that one would encounter?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: There are no villages out to the left or to the right. There is only Dalj and Borovo. But this road on the left leads to the village of Klisa -- or, rather, Vera, but that is 4 or 5 kilometres away. Not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So you told us there is only Dalj and Borovo. So just to be clear: This road going north to south, is that the Dalj to Borovo road?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, towards Dalj.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now in your statement at page 5, you tell us that you learned that the people that you had buried at -- by the Lovas farm belongs to a group of Croats who had been brought from Vukovar and who were held in the IPK hangars. Now I would like to ask you, were you present when the people were brought at the hangars in Dalj?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And could you tell us how these people were brought from Dalj?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: To Dalj or from Dalj?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: How these people were brought to Dalj from Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: By bus. By buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Could you tell us how many buses you saw?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I would say that there were about ten buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And when these buses were brought to Dalj, you tell us that they were brought to hangars of IPK Dalj, how many hangars are we talking about here?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: How many hangars there were?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: There were four hangars.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And were you there when people were taken from the buses into the hangars?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And can you tell us who was overseeing this operation?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: The army was overseeing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And did you see any members of the army?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. They were there by the buses when they were getting out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And can you tell us how were people taken into the hangars? How was this organised?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as the buses arrived, the men were taken to one hangar and the women to another.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. The last topic that I would like to deal with is -- well, slightly related to this. You explained to us that the people held in the hangars were held for one night. Do you know where these people were taken on the following day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, on the following day they went to Novi Sad. That's what they said. To the SPENS hall.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now during the rest of 1991 and during the course of 1992, to your knowledge, were there other operations whereby Croats were transported out of Dalj?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Were there situations where Croats left Dalj?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I think there were some who went to Osijek for Christmas, or, rather, they were driven out. That was the second time. Driven out by those who were -- played prominent roles in Dalj.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And can you explain to the Trial Chamber how they were driven out?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, at Christmas for some reason, for the purpose of looting and because of the houses, it was necessary for all the Croats to be driven out of their houses and taken to Osijek. This was organised. They were taken there by bus. They were put on the buses and driven to Osijek.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: How did you learn about this?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was well known. One could see the buses that were there, and people went to the Croatian houses and forced them to get on the buses and go to Osijek.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And you say that this was done by people who played prominent roles in Dalj. Did you see on those occasions who these people were?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: No, I couldn't see who they were. Pajo and his close associates, his assistants, were those who were most important there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: That's all I ask, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. The last exhibit, Mr. Demirdjian, the Registrar tells me that it is MFI'd. No?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: It --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, I see it here. It says "marked for identification." But I was asking to tender it in full. I think that perhaps we were expecting more markings at the time, but we can tender it in full at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Witness, Mr. Miladinovic, I just want to clarify something. In the transcript, page 59, line 40 -- or lines 40 to 44, you mention the army that was overseeing the operation that was taking people out of the buses and placing them in hangars. Which army are we speaking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the army that was in Vukovar. The regular army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you remind me what the name of this regular army is, in fact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand what you mean when you say "what was its name."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was it -- well, in fact, each army has a name. What kind of force was present there? It belonged to which government, in fact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it was the JNA, the Yugoslav Peoples' Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. -- or good afternoon, Mr. Miladinovic. My name is Christopher Gosnell. I represent Mr. Hadzic and I will be asking you just a few questions. If there is anything that is not clear, please ask me for further clarification or specification. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness be asked to move closer to the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, the interpreters are asking whether you could speak -- perhaps you could move the microphone closer to your mouth. Now, sir, just to pick up on the last subject that you were being asked about by the Prosecutor, and this was some Croats being forced out at around Christmas time, according to you. Do you remember us just speaking about that a couple of minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you recall that when you were speaking to the Prosecutor before your testimony that you recalled that this was actually around Easter 1992 and not Christmas. Is it correct that it was Easter 1992 that this occurred?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly whether it was Christmas or Easter. I think it was Easter. I don't know for sure but I know it was holiday time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Back in August 1991 or the summer of 1991, you say that you knew that there was an attack coming against Dalj. How long before the attack occurred did you know that that was going to occur?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: That day, in the evening, around 6.00, 7.00 p.m. already, the whole village already knew from those people who travelled constantly to Borovo and Dalj. We heard it from them. The story spread around the village and people talked, of course, and everybody soon knew there would be an attack at such and such a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So it was just the day before that you learned of this impending attack on Dalj; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: That same day around this -- around 6.00, 7.00 p.m., and the attack came the next day. Yes. So it was the day before.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Amongst Serbs, what political parties were active in the summer of 1991?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: The SDS and the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And the HDZ would be a party to which Croats primarily were members, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Was there any party other than the SDS on the Serbian side?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And what percentage of - and I know you can't be exact, and that's fine - but what percentage of the adult population, as best you can surmise based on what you knew at the time, were members of the SDS? Was it a high percentage or a low percentage?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I think at that time the SDS had a higher percentage.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Would you say that you knew very many people who were members of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean by did I know them. Almost all the Serbs were affiliated with the SDS. You didn't have to know somebody personally. If you knew he was a Serb, he was in the SDS or a follower of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Earlier today at page 50 of your testimony you referred to some individuals from the SDS in Bogojevo coming to Dalj on the second day after the attack. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: No. From Bogojevo, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, let me read out what you said and perhaps a correction is in order.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So the question that you were asked at page 50 was: "Can you tell us when you heard that Stricevic was put in charge of interrogations? "A. Yes. Well, that was on the second day. When those people from the SDS came from Bogojevo, they immediately set upon deciding who is going to be whom in the village." Was that answer -- was that what you said, or was perhaps your answer inaccurately recorded?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Not from Bogojevo, from Borovo. From Borovo. Those people came and the important positions were immediately filled. Nobody from Bogojevo had anything to do with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And when you say "those people," does that include Pavle Milovanovic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now you mentioned during your testimony at page 46 a certain Djordje Calosevic who becomes, according to you, the president of the Dalj municipality. Do you remember that, referring to him as the president of the Dalj municipality?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you remember that he assumed that position after the creation of the RSK?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: He was immediately appointed to the top position in the municipality, president of the municipality. The other one was the commander of the village. And these people elected each other, those people who had come from Borovo as refugees who did not dare stay in Dalj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And by "immediately," you mean immediately after the 1st of August when Dalj was taken over by the JNA and the TO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Are you sure that there was a municipality in existence at that time in August, September, October?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I think it immediately became a municipality at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You also refer in your statement and in your testimony to a Calosevic who had a nickname Fafrika. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that this Fafrika is different from the Djordje Calosevic who later became president of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you remember whether -- do you remember Fafrika's first name?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Zoran Calosevic, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Earlier today you testified at page 50 that -- you were asked what percentage of non-Serbs left Dalj at the time of its take-over by the JNA and the TO. And you said that 90 per cent left. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you said that they were taken away on a boat from Aljmas; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, did these village leave Dalj after Dalj -- after control of Dalj had been assumed by the JNA and the TO or did they leave in advance of the control being seized by the JNA and the TO?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: They left before. Let me explain. When the attack began, they left - all of them - as a group. It was probably organised before that they should leave as soon as the attack begins. From Aljmas to Osijek, they got onto a trailer-truck or several trailer-trucks and went to Osijek.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And was the ZNG or the Croatian police involved in organising this movement of Croatian civilians from Dalj to Aljmas?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: That I don't know. Really.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you know whether there was any co-ordination or agreement between the JNA and anyone on the Croatian side in respect of this organised evacuation?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: At page 2 of your statement you say, and I quote: "When we had to go to work in the fields, we had to get a permit from the TO Dalj. At that time, the TO was practically fully controlling the life in the village." Now can you tell us, please, in a little bit more detail in concrete terms how you mean that the TO was fully controlling life in the village?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: They were like the authorities. Everything you wanted to get done, you had to report it to them first so that they should know where we are, what we are doing, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: How long did that situation last that the TO was fully controlling the life in the village?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: They were always in control, except that later the JNA took over control of the entire area. But they remained in their role as the main authority along with the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, did you get a sense that sometime in 1992 there was a greater civilian presence in Dalj?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: No, not particularly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Was the TO controlling the police in Dalj from August 1991 through to the end of the year?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were in charge of everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now you say in your statement at paragraph 10, which is on page 3 --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And this is my informal paragraph numbering, I don't think anyone else has it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- that you learned that Zeljko Cizmic was appointed as the Dalj milicija commander. How did you come to learn that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Everything that went on immediately became common knowledge. You could hear Tom was appointed, this Dick was appointed, that Harry was appointed the other thing. It's a small village. People talk.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Okay. Is it safe to say that that's also how you knew that these other individuals listed on page 3 as members of the police, the Trbic brothers, Sinisa Glodic, Gojsovic, you learned this through word of mouth that they were members of the police?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now just looking at page 3 of your statement, you list these members of the police, the Dalj police, and then you say: "Later on I learned that Milorad Stricevic was put in charge of the interrogations of non-Serb villagers who remained in Dalj and the surrounding villages." And then you list Milinkovic, Gojsovic, the brothers Trbic, Sinisa Glodic, as people who assisted Milorad Stricevic with his work.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So as far as you knew, is it fair to say that the police was co-ordinating with Stricevic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that was so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you know whether Cizmic was also helping Mr. Stricevic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And was he also participating in these interrogations of non-Serb villagers?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: That I couldn't say. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, how do you know that these particular individuals listed in your statement, how do you know that they were assisting Stricevic with these interrogations?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: They had vehicles. They went around and brought people into custody. You could see them driving around the village. They had some sort of power compared to ordinary citizens in villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you know where these interrogations were taking place?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: In the centre of Dalj at the Dom. You know, I can't remember now. What is it? The hall of culture. It's a large building and that's where they were stationed, where he had his offices.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Is that where the TO headquarters was located?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Is that also where Cizmic was based?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Cizmic was at the police station because Dalj has a police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: How far from the police station was the Dom Kulture?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: About 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you ever learn that there was a detention facility of any sort in the Zadruga building near the Orthodox church?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I heard there was something there, but who was held inside, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: When did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: As the days went by after the attack, people who had some sort of power, they were looking for office space, and that's how we learned -- we learned who was where.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure that I understand your answer. Did anyone tell you that there was such a facility?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: It's not that anyone specifically told me. All of this was within the centre, about 100 metres from the Dom. It was in plain sight and you could also hear and see that there are some people there, that they are moving about. Later on we also learned that there was some sort of prison there, too, that some people were held inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you know who was running that facility or in control of that facility?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you know whether Stricevic was interrogating individuals there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, he had his office at the Dom. It was not actually a proper office, it was some sort of room, where he questioned people.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I believe you said earlier today -- well, first of all, I'll ask you to confirm: Do you know that these interrogations included beatings?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I heard that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: All right. And did you hear that Stricevic beat people in his office at the TO?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I told you, from what we heard from people who were closer to it all, he was doing that. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I suppose my question is this: Would it have been easier to conceal beatings at the Zadruga detention location than to conceal them in the TO headquarters, based on what you know of where people lived and how close people were to these various locations?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know whether ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did it appear to you that Cizmic and Milovanovic were in a relationship of subordinate to superior?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know which one of them was superior to the other. They collaborated. I know that much. But which of them had the higher position, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now you say at page 4 of your statement that you learned that the Lovas farm, located by the road between Savulja and Dalj, was taken over by the TO from Borovo Selo. Do you remember having said that the farm was taken over by the TO from Borovo Selo?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Can you just explain for us why it was the Borovo Selo TO that took over the farm rather than the Dalj TO?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Since it was them who liberated us, then they took over the property.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Why didn't those who were running the Dalj TO take over the Lovas farm?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: At page 3 of your statement, you describe -- well, actually, it's at page 4 of your statement, you say that: "One day Djordje Calosevic arrived with a truck and brought four elderly Croats from Dalj prison ... to dig a grave." And you spoke a little about that earlier today. Can you recall how long before the fall of Vukovar that event occurred?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand what you're driving at. What do you mean "before the fall"?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, we've heard other evidence in the case that suggests that Vukovar was -- fell, was defeated by the JNA and other forces on or around the 19th of November, and I'm sure that you recall this event. Do you remember Vukovar falling?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Okay. So my question is: In relation to this event where Djordje Calosevic shows up with some elderly prisoners to bury a grave, how long before the fall of Vukovar did that occur?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly but perhaps ten days before the fall of Vukovar. While the fighting was still ongoing for Vukovar, it was in that same period, perhaps ten days before.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You say that you later learned that Arkan was responsible for killing these individuals. Do you know whether at the time Arkan was participating in this --

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you know whether at the time that he killed these individuals he was participating in the attack on Vukovar? Did you hear that as well or did you not hear that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now you say here that Calosevic brought four elderly Croats from Dalj prison. What place are you referring to when you say "Dalj prison"?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: There, at the Dom, next to Stricevic. There was also a large room next door like a detention facility where he interrogated people.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And that's where those elderly prisoners came from?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know where they came from. I believe they were local people from surrounding villages. I'm not sure but I think they were residents of the surrounding villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You were asked how far Lovas farm is from Dalj. Approximately how far is Lovas farm from Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Some 6, 7 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you say that you - this is at the top of page 5 of your statement - that you "saw a man making a list or something like that. I did not know him and I also cannot describe him, but I'm sure that he was not from Dalj." Casting your mind back to that event, can you at least tell us whether he was wearing civilian clothing, or military clothing, or some combination of the two?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Civilian clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you hear him say anything?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't get off the excavator. When I arrived there I remained in the excavator. They loaded everything. So I didn't get off the excavator at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did it appear from you -- to you from your vantage point on the excavator that he was issuing orders to the other individuals who were there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So he was just standing off to one side observing; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: He was making some sort of notes. And as he was writing all these things down, these two loaded everything up and I did what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you say here at the -- in the third paragraph of page 5 that: "I also heard that these people were killed by the TO from Savulja." Can you recall who told you that they were killed by people from the Savulja TO?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, when I arrived at the farm --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since I knew them, they approached me and said that they were from Savulja, that they had waited for them there and killed them. Because there is a hangar in front and they spent the night there, and then on the following day, allegedly, they were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Witness, you said something at the very beginning of your answer that was not captured by the interpreters. Could you try to say that again, please?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: There was a guard at the farm before I arrived there. As I knew him - he is from Savulja - he showed me where there were holes, where I was to take the bodies to, and he told me about this at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And as far as you know, was the Savulja TO part of the Borovo Selo TO or was it somehow autonomous?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I think they were together in Borovo Selo.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You say in your statement at page 2 that tension was growing in early 1991 and that people were losing their jobs and being replaced by unqualified person of Croatian background, especially in the police force. Do you remember that happening?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And what exactly was going on? Who was being brought in to take these positions?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, mostly employees, workers from the reserve forces. So they were from the reserve police forces and had to work. So they were employees, Croats from work. Whoever wanted to, for example, could join up. He'd be a policeman. He didn't have to work and would be paid.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And did there come a time when it was unsafe for Serbs to go out at night-time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Can you explain why that was?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: How should I explain it? For example, most people knew everyone else, so they knew what a certain person was like, what sort of tendencies he had, and such people would receive weapons and would roam around the village with these weapons, threaten whoever they wanted to threaten. So naturally the situation wasn't safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I just have a few questions about -- further questions about the situation after Dalj was taken over by the JNA and the TO. And --

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- the Prosecution has given us a note of what you said to them in September, and what -- that note says that: "When asked whether he was asked to join the TO, he answered that he," that's you, sir, "he wasn't asked to join the TO. He answered only later when the fighting had already ceased did it become mandatory for him to join the TO." Do you remember when it was that it became mandatory for you to join the TO?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well it became mandatory about two months later, when things had quietened down, and then we had to join the JNA or the TO and the JNA had to be together. We had to go. We were called up and we had to join up, join the Territorial Defence but under the auspices of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So two months after the take-over of Dalj, which was on the 1st of August, would you agree with me that that's roughly around the end of September or the beginning of October 1991?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you recall whether you ever heard that there was a decision of the SFRY presidency that had anything to do with that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And in concrete terms, what did you do after you were called up? Were you carrying a weapon with you? Did you engage in any armed combat? What did it mean that you were called up?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I personally wasn't called up because I worked where I worked. There was a lot of work. So I didn't go anywhere for a year because I had to work, and in a certain sense, it's almost as if I had been a member of the army. How should I put it? It's as if I'd been working there or as if I'd been in the TO, but there was nothing else for me to do apart from work.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Anything in redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Just a few questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Miladinovic, at page 68 today of the transcript you were asked about the TO controlling the police force in Dalj. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now you explained that the TO was in charge of everything in the town. However, what relationship, if any, do you know -- what was the relationship between the TO and the police?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. What do you mean when you say "what was the relationship"?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Did you see the TO and the police interact?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they probably interacted since they were responsible for Dalj. They must have co-operated.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And did you see this?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I didn't get involved in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You were later on asked about the Zadruga building, and you were specifically asked whether it was easier to conceal beatings at the Zadruga building as opposed to the TO headquarters. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, first of all, can you tell us where the Zadruga building is located in Dalj?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's about a hundred metres from the police building in the direction of the Danube, and about 200 metres from the hall, so it's all very close.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And how far was the TO headquarter from the police building?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's the same because the TO was in the hall and they were all there in that hall, the TO and everyone else -- or, rather, the staff and everyone else. So it was 100 metres or 200 metres to the police, and then it was about a hundred metres from the police to the other location. So it's all in the same area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And I apologise, I have one more question to ask you in relation to the previous topic when you were asked about the TO and the police interacting, and you said that you didn't get involved in that. Now, how did you come to your conclusion earlier when you were asking -- when you were answering questions from the Defence in relation to the TO and its control over the town? How did you come to that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, whenever something was needed, Pajo had to be asked about the matter. He was the main person. And with regard to police issues, he had to be addressed as well. So Pajo was the key figure and nothing could be done without him. The police couldn't do anything without him and we in particular, the local inhabitants, could not do anything without contacting him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And when you mean that you couldn't do anything without contacting him, what was required from him to do something?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, objection. At some point questions do get a little too vague, and I think that one was extremely vague.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Let me try to rephrase, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You told us the local inhabitants couldn't do anything without contacting him. What kind of things was Mr. Milovanovic contacted about?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: What kind of topics or issues would people go to with him?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, whenever something was needed. If you want to cross over, you needed to get his authorisation. If you wanted to do something at home, if you had to perform work outside the territory of the village, you had to inform him so that they knew where you were. So it was nothing of great consequence but you had to contact him so that he knew where you were and so that he was aware of the fact that you were going somewhere and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now you told -- you answered earlier to my learned friend's questions that you joined the TO in October; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Between the attack on the 1st of August and the time you joined the TO in October, how many times did you interact with Mr. Milovanovic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't have much contact with him. It was only when necessary. For example, if someone had been killed and had to be buried, well, then on such occasions, yes, I would have contact with him. Perhaps on two or three occasions, because I worked in the company, we worked throughout the day, so I didn't have time to move around. Work started at 6.00 or 7.00 in the morning, so I didn't have much contact with him. But if he needed me, well, then, yes, he might contact me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you for answering my questions, Mr. Miladinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: That's all I ask, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Miladinovic, I have just one question of you. At page 50, line 4, of today's transcript, you answered a question about the non-Serbs who left Dalj and went to Osijek from Aljmas with that ship. My question is: Where did that ship come from? Who organised it for those people to be able to board it and go to Osijek?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. It was only later when the Croats returned that we heard that there was a ship waiting in Aljmas. And when the attack started that morning, because the area where the Croats are in a majority is a little separate, but that entire area withdrew in the direction of Aljmas, and they then boarded the ship. But I don't know who organised all of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, we thank you for your coming to The Hague to assist the Tribunal with your testimony. You are now released as a witness and the usher will escort you out of the courtroom, and we wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: We have more or less ten minutes left. Is there anything we can do for the moment? Any questions, requests, procedural matters?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next witness can start tomorrow morning. There are no procedural matters from our side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Nothing from the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 20th day of November, 2012, at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
